text:
maya: Heads-up — proposing a default canary rollout config for model v3.1. Want input on percent ramps, step durations, and guard rules before I add this to the rollout API. :eyes:
lee: sharing a draft — trying to balance safety vs time-to-100%.
lee: idea: start tiny, then exponential-ish ramps, with both time and request-based stop conditions.
sam: agree on both. also add a model-quality guard (eval set) not just infra metrics.
maya: here's the draft payload I was thinking to accept in the API (open to different shapes):
```json
{
  "strategy": "canary",
  "steps": [
    {"percent": 1,  "until": "30m"},
    {"percent": 10, "until": "2h"},
    {"percent": 50, "until": "6h"},
    {"percent": 100}
  ],
  "stop_conditions": {
    "p99_latency_ms": 250,
    "error_rate_pct": 0.5,
    "model_quality_drop_pct": 1.0
  },
  "stability_criterion": {"min_requests_per_step": 5000}
}
```
jordan: +1 to model_quality_drop_pct. Where do we compute that? nightly evals are too slow — need online eval hooks or a small shadow eval set that runs alongside the canary traffic.
sam: we already have telemetry that computes per-request quality score for a few label sets. Could reuse that for a rolling window check.
lee: question: should the API allow "until": "stable" meaning "advance when metrics stable for X minutes" vs fixed durations? I prefer an opt-in 'auto-advance' mode.
maya: yes — add an explicit auto_advance flag on a step. e.g. {percent:10, auto_advance: true, stability_window: 15m} to mean advance when guards are within threshold for 15m.
jordan: also need a hard cap: if a step has both auto_advance and max_duration, it must stop after max_duration even if not stable.
sam: need to consider noisy signals: use both absolute thresholds and relative baselines (delta from control). e.g., error_rate_pct > baseline + 0.2%.
lee: UX asks: console should show current step, progress (requests and percent), and which guard is blocking advance. Also let SRE pause or abort.
maya: agreed — we should emit standardized telemetry events: rollout.step_started, rollout.step_passed, rollout.step_failed with metric snapshots. That lets dashboards power the console and alerts.
ops-alert-bot: NOTE: rollout.start detected for model:v3.1 by maya in eng-platform. Scheduled in 10m.
jordan: edge-case: A/B experiments — we should allow label/experiment_id field so traffic split maps to experiments. Also routing policy needs to prefer canary pool to avoid cross-tenant noise.
sam: implementation note: prefer request-count based step termination for bursty tiny tenants: e.g. steps can be {percent:5, until: {requests:20000}} or until time.
lee: default safe schedule proposal: [1% for 30m or 2k requests, 5% for 1h or 10k requests, 25% for 4h or 50k, 100%]. Defaults+org policy can override.
maya: default guards: p99_latency_ms <= 200ms (or baseline + 20%), error_rate <= 0.5% (or baseline + 0.3%), model_quality_drop_pct <= 0.75%.
jordan: also require a 'canary_signal' tag so observability teams can route synthetic traffic and isolate canary telemetry.
lee: minor API shape thought: allow named presets so console and CLI can pass "preset": "fast-safe" vs custom steps.
maya: good. I'll add presets in the first pass. Also adding version pinning for rollback target.
sam: testing: we need a small harness that can simulate failures and latency spikes in staging to validate stop_conditions. Otherwise defaults will be untested.
maya: scheduled: I'm going to land the API patch with presets + config shape above. Will add a beta flag and a console card for manual rollout control.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout configured for model:v3.1 by maya. Start in 10 minutes, strategy=canary, preset=fast-safe. :rocket:
ops-alert-bot: ALERT-HOOK: If any stop_condition fires during canary, an incident channel will be created and owners paged.
lee: final note — docs should call out recommended monitoring queries (p99, 5xx rate, model-quality rolling average) and quick troubleshooting steps.
maya: thanks everyone — I'll post the PR and the example dashboards. :thumbsup:
